# ai-jury

> Install once. Run a cross-vendor review jury anywhere. A small, stdlib-only Python
> CLI that orchestrates native coding-agent CLIs from different vendors (Claude Code,
> OpenAI Codex, Google Antigravity) to review the *same* diff/PR, debate each other's
> findings, verify them against the code, and synthesize one chair verdict.

Key facts:

- Language/runtime: Python ≥3.11, **zero runtime dependencies** (standard library only).
- Install: `pipx install ai-jury` once published; until then
  `pipx install git+https://github.com/berkayturanci/ai-jury.git`
  (entry point: `jury`).
- Differentiator: drives each vendor's **native CLI agent** as a headless subprocess,
  not API-level model calls. The research-backed lever is **vendor heterogeneity**.
- Panel: Universal agent provider support — Cloud CLIs (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Google Antigravity), hosted APIs (OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Groq, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini), free local open-weight models (Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio), and arbitrary coding CLI tools (`vendor = "cli"` like Aider, Goose, OpenHands).
- Pipeline: round 1 independent review → round 2 cross-examination/debate (adaptive
  early-stop) → optional verification pass → chair synthesis → one report. Large diffs
  are filtered + chunked; runs are bounded by an optional budget/retries and an optional
  result cache.
- Secure by default: reviewers run sandboxed/read-only (Codex `-s read-only`, Antigravity
  `--sandbox`, Claude write-tool denylist), since they read attacker-controlled diffs.
- Output: markdown / JSON / SARIF report; optional GitHub summary + inline comments;
  structured findings (severity/file/line); CI gating via exit code.
- Privacy: `diff-only` context by default; secret redaction on by default; local-first.

## Quickstart

- `jury init` — scaffold a `jury.toml` (detects installed agents + local models);
  `--preset offline|fast|balanced|thorough`; `--list-agents` / `--list-models`.
- `jury config show` — print the effective resolved config; `jury --doctor` — readiness + next steps.
- `jury --pr 123` — review a GitHub PR (needs `gh`).
- `git diff origin/HEAD... | jury --diff-file -` — review the current branch.
- `jury --pr 123 --auto` — auto-depth: scale rounds/verify to the diff.
- `jury --pr 123 --post --post-progress` — live sticky PR status comment per round/chunk.
- `jury --pr 123 --post --post-mode phased` — post Round 1 / debate / decision as separate comments.
- `jury --pr 123 --incremental` — review only changes since the last jury run.
- `jury --pr 123 --suggest-patches` — also emit inspectable patches for verified findings.
- `jury --mock --diff-file examples/sample.diff` — offline demo, no live CLIs.
- `jury --ci --fail-on high,critical` — gate CI on blocking findings.
- `jury comment --text "/jury review" --pr 123` — run from an allowlisted PR comment.

## Configuration

- File: `jury.toml` (`[jury]`, `[[agent]]`, `[jury.context]`, `[jury.ci]`,
  `[jury.diff]`); per-run overrides via CLI flags. Scaffold it with `jury init`.
- Key settings: `rounds` (1=review, 2=+debate), `early_stop`/`max_rounds`, `chair`,
  `timeout`, `total_timeout`/`phase_timeout`/`retries`, `verify`; per-agent
  `vendor`/`command`/`extra_args`, or for a local agent `vendor = "local"` +
  `endpoint`/`model`.
- Optional project review policy: `.jury/policy.toml` (high-risk paths, focus areas,
  severity overrides) — trusted, separate from `jury.toml`.

## Non-goals

- Not a hosted review SaaS and not a dashboard product.
- Not a general multi-agent framework — scope is cross-vendor review orchestration only.
- Does not **auto-apply** patches; `--suggest-patches` emits inspectable suggestions for
  verified findings only, never applied automatically.
